items.title: Document pressure controls
items.statement: LSPS-027 requires per-server open-document limits, didClose on eviction, capped initialize roots, debounced didChange, incremental changes when supported, and avoidance of massive initialize path lists.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The LSP client controls scale pressure by limiting open documents per server, sending didClose on buffer eviction, capping initialize roots, debouncing didChange at the default interval, preferring incremental contentChanges when supported, and avoiding thousands of initialize paths.

items.title: Pressure-control execution semantics are incomplete
items.statement: The window preserves numeric tokens for document, root, and debounce limits but does not specify eviction selection, whether limits are hard or configurable, queue/coalescing behavior, or the required full-sync fallback when incremental contentChanges are unsupported.
items.impact: Independent builders can evict different buffers, handle cap overflow differently, and produce incompatible didChange behavior under pressure.
items.builder_discretion: Eviction ordering, configuration policy, debounce edge semantics, overload behavior, and full-content fallback remain discretionary.

items.title: Fallback symbol ownership boundary
items.statement: When LSP diagnostics and symbols are unavailable, FileManager owns regex, heuristic, or indexed fallback navigation and optional install hints; the LSP client does not own that index path.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: When LSP diagnostics and symbols are unavailable, FileManager remains responsible for regex, heuristic, or indexed fallback symbol navigation and optional install hints, while the LSP client does not own the symbol index path.

items.title: Fallback activation and recovery states are undefined
items.statement: The fallback boundary does not define how partial capability loss, stale indexes, server restart, or recovery back to healthy LSP state is detected and presented.
items.impact: Consumers may expose fallback data as current semantic truth or fail to return to server-backed results consistently.
items.builder_discretion: Health detection, stale-data labeling, transition timing, and recovery reconciliation remain discretionary.

evidence.exact_quote: - Fallback symbol behavior must not claim healthy LSP diagnostics or semantic symbol state.

items.title: MVP stdio-only transport boundary
items.statement: The MVP client supports stdio transport only; TCP-only servers are reached through custom stdio bridges, while native TCP/socket support is explicitly out of scope.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The MVP LSP client speaks stdio only; TCP-only servers such as Godot are supported through custom stdio bridge commands like godot-lsp-stdio-bridge, while native TCP/socket support remains out of scope for MVP.

items.title: Bridge lifecycle and trust contract are missing
items.statement: Bridge-related exact tokens identify binary-safe buffers, automatic port discovery, candidate ports, and Windows URI normalization, but the window does not specify process launch/termination, discovery precedence, connection timeout, retry, failure reporting, command trust, or port exposure rules.
items.impact: Bridge implementations can diverge in lifecycle, error handling, URI behavior, and exposure to untrusted commands or endpoints.
items.builder_discretion: Command validation, port discovery algorithm, retry policy, shutdown semantics, and security boundary remain discretionary.

items.title: Canonical MVP operation and status envelope
items.statement: LSPS-030 preserves the operation inventory, normalized fields operation/query/path/position/newName/status, and the status values ok, partial, unavailable, and error.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The canonical MVP LSP surface preserves its operation inventory, normalized parameter fields, and result status envelope using operation, query, path, position, newName, status, and the ok, partial, unavailable, or error status values.

items.title: Operation payload and status semantics are unspecified
items.statement: The envelope names input fields and status values but does not define per-operation required/optional inputs, result payload schemas, error detail, partial-result completeness, unavailable causes, or unknown-operation behavior.
items.impact: Callers and implementations can agree on status labels while remaining wire-incompatible and interpreting partial or unavailable results differently.
items.builder_discretion: Per-operation validation, output shapes, error codes, and status semantics remain discretionary.

items.title: Rename is the sole approval-gated write operation
items.statement: Rename is write-capable and approval-gated, requires path, position, and newName, and treats lsp_rename only as a legacy alias rather than another operation.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: The write-capable rename operation is approval-gated, requires path, position, and newName, and treats lsp_rename as a legacy alias for rename rather than a second operation over the nine read-only operation surface.

items.title: Rename approval and mutation lifecycle are incomplete
items.statement: The window requires approval and later requires FileSafe-backed rename, but does not define who grants approval, what is previewed, how rejection/cancellation works, how workspace edits are validated, or what atomicity and rollback guarantees apply.
items.impact: A write-capable operation can be implemented with materially different authorization, safety, and recovery guarantees.
items.builder_discretion: Approval identity and scope, preview UX, edit validation, conflict handling, atomicity, rollback, and audit evidence remain discretionary.

evidence.exact_quote: - Rename and formatting use FileSafe-backed paths rather than direct mutation.

items.title: Phase 1 core LSP outcome
items.statement: Phase 1 includes the core client, registry, document sync, diagnostics, hover, completion, Problems integration, status UI, and explicit unavailable fallback as the foundation before later enhancements.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Phase 1 ships the core LSP client, server registry, document sync, diagnostics, hover, completion, Problems integration, status UI, and explicit fallback behavior as the foundation before navigation and chat enhancements.

items.title: Phase 1 has explicit user-visible integration
items.statement: Problems integration and LSP status UI are explicitly user-visible Phase 1 surfaces, and fallback remains visible behavior when no server is available.

items.title: Phase sequencing is prose-only
items.statement: Phase 1 is described as the foundation before Phase 2, yet LSPS-032 and LSPS-033 both declare empty dependencies and unblocks, leaving the enforceable transition gate and readiness criteria unspecified.
items.impact: Phase 2 work can be treated as independently ready despite the stated foundation ordering.
items.builder_discretion: The completion gate between phases and which Phase 1 capabilities must be operational first remain discretionary.

items.title: Phase 2 editor, settings, and Chat expansion
items.statement: Phase 2 adds navigation, editing, inlay and semantic features, code actions, code lens, signature help, timeout/cancellation, server enablement controls, Settings, bridge usage, Chat LSP, and diagnostics context.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Phase 2 adds editor navigation and editing features, inlay and semantic features, code actions and code lens, signature help, timeout/cancellation, per-server enable/disable, Settings > LSP, bridge pattern, Chat LSP, and diagnostics for Assistant/Interview context.

items.title: Phase 2 GUI consumers are named
items.statement: Settings > LSP and Chat LSP are explicit GUI-facing consumers, with diagnostics intended for Assistant/Interview context.

items.title: Phase 2 operational and propagation contracts are absent
items.statement: The broad Phase 2 inventory does not define timeout values, cancellation state/result semantics, enable/disable persistence and restart behavior, Chat request/response contracts, diagnostic selection limits, or propagation freshness and privacy boundaries for Assistant/Interview context.
items.impact: Editor, Settings, Chat, and Assistant consumers can observe inconsistent behavior and may propagate excessive or stale diagnostic data.
items.builder_discretion: Timeout policy, cancellation semantics, settings persistence, Chat schema, diagnostic filtering, freshness, and privacy treatment remain discretionary.

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: Phase 2 adds editor navigation and editing features, inlay and semantic features, code actions and code lens, signature help, timeout/cancellation, per-server enable/disable, Settings > LSP, bridge pattern, Chat LSP, and diagnostics for Assistant/Interview context.

items.title: Plan migration and index validation are explicit
items.statement: Each unit names plan migration validation and plan index validation as its validation surfaces.

items.title: Runtime acceptance oracles are missing
items.statement: The acceptance criteria and validation surfaces prove source preservation and plan indexing, but provide no executable oracle for document caps, sync behavior, fallback truth, bridge transport, operation envelopes, approval gating, GUI status, cancellation, or phase outcomes.
items.impact: The units can pass their named validators while none of the specified LSP behavior has been demonstrated.
items.builder_discretion: Test fixtures, observable outcomes, failure injections, latency thresholds, GUI assertions, and phase-exit criteria remain unspecified.

evidence.exact_quote: - The covered source span remains losslessly available for exact-text audit.

items.title: Planning units do not create executable work
items.statement: The window explicitly prevents these planning units from creating WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, or production build tasks.

evidence.exact_quote: - No WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, or production build tasks are created.

items.title: Owner boundaries are explicit
items.statement: Plans/LSPSupport.md owns LSP protocol/client constraints, while FileManager explicitly owns fallback navigation where applicable.

evidence.exact_quote: - Plans/FileManager.md owns fallback symbol navigation; Plans/LSPSupport.md owns the LSP unavailable boundary.
- Plans/LSPSupport.md owns LSP-specific protocol/client constraints while referenced owner docs retain their SSOT boundaries.

items.title: Legacy rename alias migration is resolved
items.statement: lsp_rename is explicitly retired as an independent operation and retained only as a legacy alias for rename.

evidence.exact_quote: - lsp_rename must not become a second operation distinct from rename.
- The packetization label `10 read-only + 1 write-gated (lsp_rename)` is reconciled by treating `lsp_rename` as a legacy alias.

items.title: Unavailable-server fallback is mandatory
items.statement: Phase 1 explicitly requires fallback behavior when no server is available.

evidence.exact_quote: - Phase 1 must retain explicit fallback behavior when no server is available.

dimension_assessments.summary: Core behaviors are named across scale control, fallback, transport, operations, rename, and phased feature outcomes, with execution gaps separately recorded.
Phase 1 and Phase 2 capability inventories are explicit.
Normalized input field names and status values exist, but per-operation input requirements and output payloads are absent.
Transport, alias, and status-envelope contracts are explicit; bridge, operation-payload, and write-safety contracts remain incomplete.
Fallback and phase transitions are described but lack enforceable state machines and readiness gates.
FileManager/LSP and rename approval boundaries are named, but the approving principal and scope are not.
The owner document and the FileManager fallback boundary are explicit.
FileManager, editor, Problems, Settings, Chat, Assistant, and Interview consumers are identifiable in the window.
Problems, status UI, Settings, and Chat are explicit GUI surfaces, but user-visible states, actions, errors, and approval presentation are not specified.
Unavailable fallback is mandatory, while recovery from fallback, bridge failure, cancellation, and write failure remains unspecified.
Approval gating provides a safety boundary, but bridge command trust and diagnostic propagation privacy are not defined.
Diagnostics are intended for Problems and Assistant/Interview consumers, but selection, freshness, limits, and stale-data propagation are unspecified.
The operation inventory and bridge pattern are named, but lifecycle, retries, timeout/cancellation semantics, and per-operation behavior are incomplete.
Caps and debounce tokens address pressure, while eviction, coalescing, overload, and measurable performance oracles remain open.
The stdio bridge compatibility strategy and lsp_rename alias retirement are explicit.
Plan-shape validators are named, but behavioral and runtime acceptance oracles are absent.
Consequential discretion remains across eviction, fallback transitions, bridge trust/lifecycle, payload schemas, write safety, phase gates, settings, Chat propagation, and executable tests.
The review found bounded ambiguities in operational semantics and acceptance, while ownership, MVP transport scope, alias disposition, and non-creation of executable work are explicit non-gaps.
